?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:165636
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 35855 of 2023

Applicant :- Chotu @ Sajid
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Parvez Alam
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Parvez Alam, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur,
learned AGA for the State.
2. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 0052 of 2023, under Sections 376, 323, 506 IPC, Police Station Rorawar, District Aligarh during pendency of the trial.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant under Section 376 IPC and according to the FIR when informant arrived at spot after hearing the shriek of his wife then found that applicant was running from her room and his wife stated that applicant committed rape with her.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant in the FIR as well as in both the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. is totally false and baseless and actually prosecutrix i.e. victim is major and married lady and applicant is her neighbor and she was having illicit relationship with the applicant but when her Chotu @ Sajid vs State Of U.P. on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21892546/
1 husband witnessed the applicant in her room then he lodged the FIR of the present case.

5. He further submits that although during investigation prosecutrix in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant but when she appeared before the trial court then she did not support the prosecution case and has declared hostile.

He further submits that informant of the case i.e. husband of the prosecutrix has also declared hostile during trial and statement of both informant and prosecutrix has been annexed along with supplementary affidavit.
He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 06.02.2023.
6. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
7. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. Although, during investigation prosecutrix in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C made allegation of rape against the applicant but prosecutrix is major and married lady and argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant and prosecutrix were having relationship cannot be completely brushed aside.
Further, from the record it also reflects that during trial when informant and prosecutrix appeared before the trial court then both have declared hostile.

9. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant - Chotu @ Sajid be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
